name: Chodos and Detweiler's five-dimensional universe
description: Three expanding spatial circles and one contracting circle in a five-dimensional vacuum universe.
convention: We use signature $(-,+,+,+,+)$ and keep $c$ explicit. Cosmic time $t$, the equality time $t_0$ and the normalization time $\tau$ have units of time; $L$ and the spatial coordinates have units of length. Tensor components use $x^0=ct$.
history: Every spatial direction closes into a circle in the universe Alan Chodos and Steven Detweiler studied in 1980 [chodos1980, chyba1985]. At the reference time $t_0$, each circuit has the same proper length $L$. Three circles expand as cosmic time advances, while the fourth contracts. The vacuum field equations hold in five spacetime dimensions throughout [chyba1985]. ¶ Their cosmology belongs to the higher-dimensional Kasner family, whose spatial scale factors are powers $(t/t_0)^{p_i}$ [chyba1985]. The four spatial exponents obey $\sum_i p_i=\sum_i p_i^2=1$. The choice $p_1=p_2=p_3=1/2$ and $p_5=-1/2$ makes the three expanding directions locally isotropic. Christopher F. Chyba set out this construction in his 1985 account of Kaluza-Klein unification [chyba1985]. ¶ At cosmic time $t$, the three growing circumferences are $L\sqrt{t/t_0}$ and the fifth-direction circumference is $L\sqrt{t_0/t}$ [chyba1985]. Their ratio is $t/t_0$, so a late universe can have three macroscopic spatial directions and a much smaller closed direction. Toward the initial singularity at $t=0$, the three expanding circles shrink to zero and the fourth circumference grows without bound [chodos1980, chyba1985]. ¶ A constant spatial coordinate rescaling normalizes all four spatial metric coefficients to one at a chosen time $\tau$ [chyba1985]. The coordinate periods then become $L\sqrt{\tau/t_0}$ in the three growing directions and $L\sqrt{t_0/\tau}$ in the fifth. The proper circumferences continue to depend on the cosmic time $t$. Equal metric coefficients at one instant coexist with unequal circuit lengths. ¶ Chodos and Detweiler related the small fifth circumference to quantized charge by perturbing the metric and imposing periodicity on a scalar quantum field [chodos1980, chyba1985]. They treated $t/\tau$ as approximately constant during that calculation [chyba1985]. The cosmological vacuum itself keeps the fifth circle contracting as $t^{-1/2}$. The three equal positive exponents and one negative exponent select this evolution; Chyba emphasized that the field equations admit other choices [chyba1985].

related.text: The four spatial exponents are $(1/2,1/2,1/2,-1/2)$, with each spatial direction closed into a circle [chyba1985].
Its five-dimensional vacuum chart has these local scale factors at $s_1=s_2=s_3=1/2$ and $s_5=-1/2$. The four spatial coordinates here are periodic [chyba1985].
The proper size of a compact direction varies with position in the monopole and with cosmic time in this vacuum universe.

coordinates.name: Synchronous

parameters.description: Positive cosmic time at which all four proper circumferences equal $L$
Common positive coordinate period in the synchronous chart, with units of length

coordinates.convention: The source's spatial coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3,x^5$ are written $x,y,z,w$. The four proper circumferences equal $L$ at $t=t_0$.

coordinates.name: Rescaled

parameters.description: Positive cosmic time at which all four proper circumferences equal $L$
Common positive coordinate period in the synchronous chart, with units of length
Fixed positive cosmic time at which the rescaled spatial metric coefficients equal one

coordinates.convention: The rescaling is $X=\sqrt{\tau/t_0}x$, $Y=\sqrt{\tau/t_0}y$, $Z=\sqrt{\tau/t_0}z$ and $W=\sqrt{t_0/\tau}w$, with $t$ unchanged.
